objective: Independent security review of PR2's new PostToolUse hook on the Agent tool and the changed SessionStart composition.
acceptance_criteria: Assesses whether a payload can write outside the state directory, poison verify for another agent id, or create state for non-holyclaude agents; whether stdin handling is bounded and fails safe; whether the new hooks.json entry widens what runs.
Assesses whether the SessionStart change can drop or truncate the core rules in a way that matters.
Each finding traced source to sink with severity, or none.
result: PR2 security review: no critical/high/medium; low L1 no stdin or field cap (stuck log only past the 4 MiB local cap), L2 requested type overwrites observed type, L3 hook model masks a mid-run model change, L4 resume relabel suspicion removed by the L2 fix; SessionStart change cannot drop rules and stays within the budget.

acceptance.rationale: Traced payload sources to the log sink and verify; read-only limits stated.

criteria_evidence.Assesses whether a payload can write out: No outside writes, id from Claude Code, gate before writes, same exec form; stdin unbounded (L1).
criteria_evidence.Assesses whether the SessionStart change: Rules cut only past the budget, else whole.
